bio.headline: Forged between code and equations
bio.para1: Graduated in Computer Science with a Master's in Mathematics and Computer Science from the University of Cantabria. After several years as a software developer, I spent five years in research and university teaching before working independently, combining education and consulting.
bio.para2: For over seven years I have been helping students and professionals strengthen their skills in programming, mathematics and artificial intelligence — from academic support and learning from scratch to technical interview preparation and real-world project development.

bag-of-words.vocabSize: Corpus vocabulary: <count></count> entries, one per column.
bag-of-words.tableCaption: Bag-of-words matrix: one row per token holding its one-hot vector, one row with each document's sum, and a last row with the sum over the whole corpus.
bag-of-words.explainer: Every green row is a token's one-hot: a single <one></one>, in the column of its entry. The amber row adds them up, and that sum is the document vector; the last row adds the two documents together, which is something else. Swap two words around: the rows reorder and the sums do not move.
bag-of-words.truncated: Only the first {max} tokens of each document are shown.

embedding-projection.loadError: The embeddings could not be loaded.
embedding-projection.analogyAria: 2D projection of words showing the analogy {a} minus {b} plus {c}, which lands on {answer}
embedding-projection.neighboursAria: 2D projection of words; selected: {word}, with its neighbours {neighbours}
embedding-projection.analogyNote: The two arrows are the same vector: <term>{a} − {b}</term>, applied to <word>{c}</word>, lands on <hit>{answer}</hit>. The circle marks where the sum falls; the nearest word is the answer. Zoomed in on those four words.

activation-explorer.plotAria: The {name} activation and its derivative, with the saturation regions shaded
activation-explorer.note: Red bands: the derivative ≈ 0 (saturation) — the gradient barely flows there.

perceptron-boundary.plotAria: 2D points and the neuron's decision boundary
perceptron-boundary.separable: Separable — the neuron finds a line that gets nothing wrong.
perceptron-boundary.notSeparable: Not separable — no line leaves each colour on one side, and the neuron never stops correcting itself.
perceptron-boundary.xorNote: These four points are the XOR function, the «exclusive or»: each coordinate is −1 or +1, and the class is the green one when the two differ —top left and bottom right— and the other one when they agree. Each class takes two opposite corners, which is why no line can leave one on each side. Drag a point and the line finds room again.

gradient-descent-2d.diverged: It diverges — the learning rate is too high; the path leaves the plot.

loss-landscape.plotAria: Loss surface with two minima and the descent path
loss-landscape.verdict: It falls into the minimum on the {basin} — the starting point decides the basin.

backprop-trace.groupAria: Backpropagation trace; use the arrow keys to step forwards and backwards

rnn-unrolled.groupAria: Unrolled RNN; use the arrow keys to step forwards and backwards
rnn-unrolled.diagramAria: Unrolled RNN with {steps} steps, in {mode, select, forward {forward} other {backward}} mode
rnn-unrolled.sequenceNote: The xₜ are a fixed example sequence: one made-up vector per token.
rnn-unrolled.fixedParams: Weights and bias, the same at every step:
rnn-unrolled.forwardEnters: in come the state <hprev></hprev> = {hPrev} and the token <xt></xt> = {xValue}
rnn-unrolled.forwardFirstStep: At t = 1 the recurrent contribution W<sub>hh</sub>·h<sub>0</sub> is 0: the first state comes from the token alone.
rnn-unrolled.backwardZeroMatrix: — it is the zero matrix, because h<sub>0</sub> = 0.

vanishing-gradient.plotAria: Gradient magnitude in orders of magnitude (decimal log) against the distance in steps, for a spectral radius of {rho}. At {steps} steps the gradient {verb, select, vanishes {vanishes} explodes {explodes} other {holds}}.
vanishing-gradient.note: Vertical axis: orders of magnitude (log₁₀); 0 is the size it started at. {steps} steps away, the gradient {verb, select, vanishes {vanishes} explodes {explodes} other {holds}}: ‖·‖ becomes ≈ 10<exp>{exponent}</exp> times what it was.

lstm-gates.groupAria: LSTM with gates; use the arrow keys to step forwards and backwards
lstm-gates.survivalAria: Fraction of c₁ surviving at t={t}
lstm-gates.summary: With b_f = {bf}, between <lo>{min}</lo> and <hi>{max}</hi> of what was written into c₁ reaches the end of the sequence —with no matrix in the way: just the product of the forget gates, which the network picks coordinate by coordinate—.

context-bottleneck.plotAria: Two lines against the length of the input, in orders of magnitude. The capacity of the context vector is flat at {codes} distinct messages, with {dh} coordinates of {q} levels. The number of input sentences rises 4.5 orders per token and crosses the capacity at {crossing} tokens.
context-bottleneck.legend: Vertical axis: orders of magnitude (log₁₀) of a count. <cap>▬</cap> messages that fit in c · <dem>▬</dem> distinct input sentences of that length, over a vocabulary of {vocab} entries.
context-bottleneck.readout: In {dh} coordinates of {q} levels there is room for <codes></codes> distinct messages, and that is enough for sentences of up to <upto>{crossing} tokens</upto>. Past that there are sentences to spare: at {past} tokens no decoder —not even the best possible one, trained without limit— returns more than a <ceiling></ceiling> fraction of them exactly.

attention-alignment.mapAria: Alignment map: pick an output step to see which part of the input it pulls from
attention-alignment.attentionNote: Step {step} writes <tgt>{target}</tgt> and pulls mostly from <src>{source}</src>, with a weight of {weight}. Change step: the row moves, and its sum still comes to {sum}.
attention-alignment.frozenNote: With the fixed summary, step {step} receives the state of <src>{source}</src> with weight {weight} — and so do the other {others} steps. Walk the rows and watch the bars below: they do not move.
attention-alignment.contextAria: The {d} coordinates of the context vector of step {step}: {values}.
attention-alignment.contextNote: {d} coordinates, the same as the summary had

self-attention-heatmap.inputLabel: Type a sentence (only the first {max} tokens are kept)
self-attention-heatmap.mapAria: Self-attention map: pick a position to see which others it pulls from
self-attention-heatmap.empty: Type something and the grid appears.
self-attention-heatmap.causalFirst: With the mask, position 1 has nothing behind it: <tok>{token}</tok> takes {self} on itself and {blanked} {blanked, plural, one {cell is blanked out} other {cells are blanked out}} to its right. The row sums to {sum} like all the others: what is blanked out is shared among what is left, because the mask goes in before the softmax.
self-attention-heatmap.causalOther: With the mask, position {pos}, <tok>{token}</tok>, can only look from 1 to {pos}. Its highest weight —{peak}— goes to <tgt>{target}</tgt>, and the row still sums to {sum} with {blanked} {blanked, plural, one {cell blanked out} other {cells blanked out}}.
self-attention-heatmap.projected: Position {pos}, <tok>{token}</tok>, gives its highest weight —{peak}— to <tgt>{target}</tgt>, and {self} to itself. The whole row sums to {sum}.
self-attention-heatmap.unprojected: Unprojected, position {pos}, <tok>{token}</tok>, keeps its own highest weight: {self} on itself, against {best} from the best of the rest. And it happens in all {rows} rows at once: the diagonal always wins. A layer like that hands back what came in with a tint of everything else, and has not one parameter with which to decide otherwise.
self-attention-heatmap.footnote: The vectors ({dModel} coordinates, {lexicon} words in the lexicon) and the projections —{dk} coordinates to compare with, {dv} to mix with— I set by hand for the course; there is no trained model in here.
self-attention-heatmap.footnoteMask: The dashed cells are the ones the mask blanks out.
self-attention-heatmap.footnoteUnknown: Outside the lexicon: {words} — its vector comes from a hash of its own letters, so that row says nothing.
self-attention-heatmap.footnoteTruncated: The sentence was cut at {max} tokens.

multi-head-view.inputLabel: Type a sentence (only the first {max} tokens are kept)
multi-head-view.rowsAria: Pick a position to compare it across every head

2.name: a noun looks at its determiner and its modifiers

3.name: a determiner or a modifier looks at nouns

multi-head-view.singleHeadNote: The four rules added together before one softmax: one row per position and nothing more.
multi-head-view.empty: Type something and the grids appear.
multi-head-view.verdictFlat: shares evenly among them all — this rule says nothing about this position
multi-head-view.panelIntro: What position {pos}, <tok>{token}</tok>, pulls towards in each map:
multi-head-view.footnote: The {h} heads are the {h} rules of the lexicon ({lexicon} words) from the previous lesson, one per head, and I wrote them by hand for the course. That is why each head here compares on {dk} coordinate: it is what makes a rule readable, not what a real layer uses, which splits the model's width among its heads.
multi-head-view.footnoteUnknown: Outside the lexicon: {words} — its vector comes from a hash of its own letters, so that row says nothing.
multi-head-view.footnoteTruncated: The sentence was cut at {max} tokens.

positional-encoding.mapAria: Positional encoding: {rows} positions in rows by {cols} coordinates in columns. The columns on the left oscillate every few positions and the ones on the right are almost constant.
positional-encoding.coordinateLine: Coordinate <c>{col}</c> is the {fn, select, sine {sine} other {cosine}} of pair {pair}, turning at <r>{rate}</r> radians per position: it comes back to the same place every {cycle}.
positional-encoding.valueLine:
At position

{pos}

that coordinate is {here}, and {k} positions further along it is {there}
positional-encoding.valueLineSame: —the same number: this pair turns so slowly that it does not separate the two positions—.
positional-encoding.dotHeading: What two positions {k} apart score against each other:
positional-encoding.dotNote: Move the position and that number does not move: it is {value} across the whole sentence. Change k and it changes.
positional-encoding.footnote: {rows} positions and {cols} of the coordinates, which is what fits on a screen; a model from the paper has 512. Nothing here is set by hand: it is the paper's formula and its constant {base}, and the colours give the sign —green positive, blue negative, dark near zero—.

transformer-architecture.groupAria: Transformer architecture; use the arrow keys to walk the boxes of the diagram
transformer-architecture.diagramAria: Diagram of the Transformer: on the left the encoder, with input embedding, positional encoding, multi-head self-attention, a position-wise perceptron and two add-and-layer-norm boxes, repeated N times; on the right the decoder, with masked self-attention, encoder-decoder attention that receives the keys and the values from the encoder, a position-wise perceptron, three add-and-layer-norm boxes, and a linear projection with softmax at the end. Of the fifteen boxes, only the three attention ones mix positions. Selected box: {selected}.

topics.b4l6: the query, the key and the value
topics.b5l7: the encoder, the decoder and masks

embedding-entrada.label:
Input
embedding
embedding-entrada.description: Every token of the input sentence is swapped for its vector. One row per position, and the same table for all of them.

pe-encoder.label:
Positional
encoding
pe-encoder.description: Something that depends on which position it is in is added to each row. Without this, nothing above would know the order.

atencion-encoder.label:
Multi-head
self-attention
atencion-encoder.description: Every position asks all the others and takes away a mixture of what is in them. It is the only box in this column that looks beyond its own row.

suma-norm-enc-1.label: Add and layer norm
suma-norm-enc-1.description: It adds what went into the sublayer to what came out of it and normalises the result. Each row is normalised with its own coordinates, without looking at the others.

ffn-encoder.label:
Position-wise
perceptron
ffn-encoder.description: The multilayer perceptron from block 2, two layers deep, applied to each row separately and with the same weights on all of them.

suma-norm-enc-2.label: Add and layer norm
suma-norm-enc-2.description: The second one of the layer. What leaves here is what the next encoder layer receives, and what the decoder reads at the end.

embedding-salida.label:
Output
embedding
embedding-salida.description: The same for what is written so far, shifted by one position: in each token's place goes the previous one, never itself.

pe-decoder.label:
Positional
encoding
pe-decoder.description: The same addition as in the other column, with the same formula: position 3 receives what position 3 of the input receives.

atencion-enmascarada.label:
Masked
self-attention
atencion-enmascarada.description: Self-attention with the future positions blanked out: when writing word 4 it can look from 1 to 4, and not one more.

suma-norm-dec-1.label: Add and layer norm
suma-norm-dec-1.description: The same operation as in the encoder, and there are three in this column because there are three sublayers.

atencion-cruzada.label:
Encoder-decoder
attention
atencion-cruzada.description: The attention of the previous block, whole: the queries come from what is being written, and the keys and the values from what the encoder read.

suma-norm-dec-2.label: Add and layer norm
suma-norm-dec-2.description: The second of the three, the one that closes the sublayer looking at the encoder.

ffn-decoder.label:
Position-wise
perceptron
ffn-decoder.description: The same position-wise perceptron as in the other column, with its own weights.

suma-norm-dec-3.label: Add and layer norm
suma-norm-dec-3.description: The third and last one of the decoder layer.

salida-lineal.label:
Linear projection
and softmax
salida-lineal.description: From each row's coordinates to one probability per vocabulary entry. The same projection at every position.
